prevention.title: What NASA PSI records show on prevention

findings.text: ACME CFI-G recorded 333 tests with gas fuels at 12% to 85% oxygen (measured).
ACME/Flame Design recorded 327 tests with gas fuels at 19.8% to 85% oxygen (measured).
BASS-II recorded 129 tests with solid fuels at 13.6% to 22.2% oxygen (measured).

prevention.implication: Solid-material tests in PSI stop below the 30% oxygen expected in a lunar base, so prevention findings need checking at lunar conditions.
prevention.gap: No partial-gravity combustion data is in PSI yet.
problems: finding 3 claims flames went out, but no extinction outcome is recorded for what it cites
implication uses overconfident safety language (rely on)

detection.title: What NASA PSI records show on detection

findings.text: SPICE recorded 435 tests with gas fuels at 21% oxygen (assumed cabin air).
SAME-R recorded 109 tests with solid fuels at 21% oxygen (assumed cabin air).
SAME recorded 20 tests with solid fuels at 21% oxygen (assumed cabin air).

detection.implication: Solid-material tests in PSI stop below the 30% oxygen expected in a lunar base, so detection findings need checking at lunar conditions.
detection.gap: No partial-gravity combustion data is in PSI yet.

suppression.title: Liquid fuel droplet extinction limits

findings.text: In the FLEX experiment, liquid-fuel rows with N2+CO2 extinguished as low as 14 % measured oxygen, showing suppression can work at that level.
FLEX also recorded liquid-fuel rows with N2 extinguishing at the lowest measured 12 % oxygen, indicating nitrogen dilution is effective at very low oxygen.
With N2+He diluent, FLEX observed extinction down to 13 % measured oxygen, demonstrating helium-mixed diluents can also achieve droplet extinction at low oxygen.

suppression.implication: Designs must verify that chosen diluent systems can extinguish liquid-fuel droplets at the 30 % oxygen and ≤70.3 kPa conditions expected on a lunar base.
suppression.gap: The dataset lacks extinction data for solid fuels and for partial-gravity environments.
